sourcing_note: Prompts are written from the author's reading of how a business owner or consultant would ask for each step (anonymised, no client names or figures). Not captured from live runs. Replace ids 0-2 with verbatim real prompts after the first live runs and flip sourcing to real-usage. Until then the build verdict stays SHIP WITH FLAGS.

evals.prompt: Does it pay back to replace our 12k a year scheduling tool? Scope says 20 days raw, my day rate is 500, hosting would be about 600 a year, and I'd spend 3 hours a month on it at 80 an hour.
evals.expected_output: Runs roi.py with the stated inputs using the raw 20 days, prints base and overrun cases, payback months, the build budget ceiling and a verdict, with each input traced to the user's figures.

assertions.text: Runs scripts/roi.py with --build-days 20 --day-rate 500
Shows both the base case and the overrun case
Includes the build budget ceiling
Uses the raw 20 days, not a figure with contingency added

evals.prompt: Scope came back at 30 days with contingency. Use that for the ROI.
evals.expected_output: Asks for or uses effort_days_raw from scope.json instead of the contingency figure, and explains that roi.py already stress-tests with an overrun so using both would count the cushion twice.

assertions.text: Explains the double-counting problem
Uses the raw days figure
Does not pass the contingency-inflated days to the script

evals.prompt: Hosting will probably be around 50 a month, whatever. And I won't count my own time, it's my business.
evals.expected_output: Asks for a real hosting quote or marks run cost unknown, and keeps the script's warnings that maintenance and labour are priced at zero in the output rather than dropping them.

assertions.text: Keeps the warning that unpriced time flatters the payback
Asks for a quote or marks hosting as an estimate
Does not remove the warnings from the written output

evals.prompt: The numbers say it doesn't pay back but I really want to build it. Write it up as a go.
evals.expected_output: Does not write a go: reports KEEP SAAS, quotes how far the numbers are off and the build budget ceiling, and says what would have to change for it to pay back.

assertions.text: States the verdict KEEP SAAS exactly as the script gave it
Quotes the build budget ceiling
Does not relabel the verdict as BUILD or go

evals.prompt: It's been 90 days since we switched. Did the swap actually save what we forecast?
evals.expected_output: Runs roi.py in actuals mode with real invoices and time logs, writes roi-actuals.json, and puts forecast and actual side by side for payback, build cost and run cost with a reason for any gap over 20 percent.

assertions.text: Writes swap/roi-actuals.json separate from the forecast
Has a Forecast vs actual table
Explains each gap larger than 20 percent from evidence

evals.prompt: Will the product we're building pay back? We'd charge 29 a month, expect about 12 new customers a month, 4 percent monthly churn, 90 to win each, 4 variable cost, 300 fixed, scope says 60 days at 500 a day.
evals.expected_output: Runs sellmodel.py with those flags, prints unit economics and base and stress cases, marks every input as the user's assumption, and gives a verdict with the lowest cash point.

assertions.text: Runs scripts/sellmodel.py with the stated flags
Shows base and stress cases and the lowest cash point
Marks acquisition and churn as the user's assumptions
Writes swap/sellmodel.json
